lead: Veteran actor Olu Jacobs died, after years of false reports of his death, and the Federal Government paid tribute to his legacy. The National Assembly sent the sixth constitution amendment bill to the state assemblies, and the Supreme Court reserved judgment on INEC's appeal over the Electoral Act. A court let Atiku Abubakar serve his certificate suit on President Tinubu through the APC, ASUU began an indefinite strike at three Lagos state universities, and the outgoing Operation Hadin Kai commander said 1,106 terrorists were killed in 17 months.

items.h: Veteran actor Olu Jacobs dies
items.s: Olu Jacobs, the Nollywood veteran whose death had been falsely reported online several times, died on Wednesday. The Federal Government said his legacy will never fade.

items.h: Constitution amendment bill sent to state assemblies
items.s: The National Assembly transmitted the Sixth Alteration Bill 2026 to the 36 state Houses of Assembly and asked for their decisions within 30 days.

items.h: Supreme Court reserves judgment on Electoral Act appeal
items.s: The court reserved judgment in INEC's appeal against a Court of Appeal ruling that voided provisions of the Electoral Act 2026.

items.h: Court lets Atiku serve certificate suit on Tinubu through APC
items.s: The Federal High Court in Abuja granted Atiku Abubakar's request to serve documents in his certificate forgery suit on President Tinubu through the APC.

items.h: ASUU begins indefinite strike at three Lagos state universities
items.s: The union's joint campus group declared an indefinite strike across the three Lagos State-owned universities, including LASU.

items.h: Commander says 1,106 terrorists killed in Borno in 17 months
items.s: Outgoing Operation Hadin Kai commander Maj.-Gen. Abdulsalam Abubakar said troops killed more than 1,106 Boko Haram and ISWAP fighters, including key commanders, during his tenure.

items.h: Tinubu orders 95% NIN coverage by December
items.s: With 142 million people enrolled, the President directed the identity commission to reach 95 per cent coverage by December 2026.

items.h: IGP visits Plateau as three vigilantes are killed
items.s: Inspector-General Olatunji Disu visited Plateau after recent killings and promised stronger operations. Three vigilantes were killed in NTV community, Barkin Ladi, on Tuesday night.

items.h: Sanusi says he was wrong to delay telcos' entry into finance
items.s: Former CBN governor Sanusi Lamido Sanusi admitted he erred in holding back telecommunications companies from financial services.

items.h: Dangote promises retail investors priority if IPO is oversubscribed
items.s: Aliko Dangote said small investors will be allocated first if demand exceeds the offer, and banks reported heavy traffic on their subscription channels.

items.h: PDP picks Abacha's son as Kano governorship candidate
items.s: The Kano PDP affirmed Muhammad Sani Abacha as its candidate after Muhammad Bello Dalha withdrew.

items.h: Shettima says only six northern governors backed Tinubu in 2023
items.s: Speaking in Kwara, the Vice President said Tinubu forgave the northern governors who did not support him and urged reconciliation.

items.h: Rift between Wike and APC governors deepens
items.s: An APC group accused Wike of dividing the party, while his PDP allies said his support is for Tinubu, not the APC, and accused the governors of underperforming.

items.h: Adebayo warns petrol could reach N5,000 under a second Tinubu term
items.s: SDP candidate Adewole Adebayo made the claim while campaigning.

items.h: APM says regional commission funds could sway votes
items.s: The Allied Peoples Movement said the President's order to release money to regional commissions risks misuse before the election.

items.h: ADC and APC trade blame over Kaduna attacks
items.s: The ADC said its supporters were attacked at a toll gate, and the Kaduna APC condemned attacks on its members and offices and asked police to investigate.

items.h: Six SDP supporters die in Nasarawa crash
items.s: Supporters of governorship candidate Mohammed Adamu died in a road accident on Monday, police said.

items.h: Oba of Benin backs continuity
items.s: Oba Ewuare II told APC campaign chief Abdulaziz Yari there is no point in change for its own sake.

items.h: 'Arewa for Asiwaju' group to be unveiled
items.s: Shekarau, Geidam and Lalong lead a coalition of northern leaders preparing to launch a pro-Tinubu platform.

items.h: APC and ADC field the most National Assembly candidates
items.s: INEC data showed the APC has the most House candidates and the ADC the most Senate candidates.

items.h: Solar mini-grid commissioned at Yakubu Gowon University
items.s: The government opened a 3.3MW hybrid mini-grid with 2MWh of storage at the former University of Abuja.

items.h: Power minister asks EFCC to tackle vandalism and energy theft
items.s: Joseph Tegbe urged the commission to act against rising theft and vandalism in the electricity sector.

items.h: Farm produce inflation reaches 21.99%, highest this year
items.s: Inflation for farm produce climbed to 21.99 per cent in August, its peak for 2026 and a reversal of the slowdown seen in May.

items.h: Stocks gain N650bn as market value hits N158trn
items.s: The All-Share Index rose 0.41 per cent and market capitalisation reached N158.399 trillion.

items.h: JAMB moves 2027 UTME first-session arrival to 7.30am
items.s: The board changed arrival and exam times for the first session, citing safety and logistics.

items.h: Tinubu makes ending child labour a national priority
items.s: The President urged governors, employers and communities to act against child labour.

items.h: Kano anti-corruption commission chairman resigns
items.s: Saidu Yahaya stepped down as head of the state's anti-corruption commission, and the Kwankwasiyya movement blamed government interference.

items.h: Kano police recover 12 stolen cars and arrest 10
items.s: Police broke up a suspected interstate car theft ring operating in Kano and neighbouring states.

items.h: Seven kidnap victims rescued in Benue
items.s: Troops, police and vigilantes freed seven people from a kidnappers' hideout in Ohimini.

items.h: PenCom extends verification deadline to 31 December
items.s: More than 118,000 federal workers had not enrolled in the mandatory online exercise.

items.h: Airlines blame congestion and weather for delays
items.s: Operators said most delays and cancellations are caused by airport congestion, poor infrastructure and weather.

items.h: CAC proposes single beneficial ownership database
items.s: The Corporate Affairs Commission called for centralised ownership records to fight corruption and money laundering.

items.h: Kwara governor turbanned as Sardauna
items.s: Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq was formally turbanned in Ilorin on Wednesday.

items.h: Zamfara governor to attend UN General Assembly
items.s: Dauda Lawal will seek investment for the state at the 81st session in New York.

items.h: Nairobi beats London, Munich and Rome to 2029 World Athletics hosting
items.s: Kenya's capital will be the first African city to host the championships.

items.h: World Bank names Michael Kremer chief economist
items.s: President Ajay Banga appointed the Nobel laureate as chief economist.
